title: Respond to the failing part of the ML loop
description: Inject an incident and choose a response. A good action contains user impact while preserving the evidence needed for a durable correction.

incidents.label: Training-serving skew
incidents.detail: A feature transformation changed online but not in training.
incidents.signal: Parity mismatches rise and scores shift immediately after a feature release.
incidents.cause: The deployed model receives feature semantics it was not evaluated with.

incidents.label: Inference saturation
incidents.detail: Peak traffic pushes p99 latency beyond the decision deadline.
incidents.signal: Queue depth, saturation, timeouts, and fallback use rise together.
incidents.cause: The request path has less capacity than peak demand requires.

incidents.label: Concept drift
incidents.detail: The relationship between features and outcomes changes gradually.
incidents.signal: Delayed quality and calibration worsen while schemas and service health remain stable.
incidents.cause: The production population no longer follows the relationship learned by the model.

incidents.label: Outcome join failure
incidents.detail: Exposure identifiers are missing from a new product surface.
incidents.signal: Join coverage falls even though prediction volume remains normal.
incidents.cause: Outcomes can no longer be attributed to the policy and prediction that produced them.

responses.label: Roll back the incompatible release
responses.detail: Restore the last compatible feature and model contract, then replay parity tests.

responses.label: Activate fallback and add capacity
responses.detail: Protect the deadline first, then scale and profile the saturated path.

responses.label: Build fresh evidence and retrain
responses.detail: Validate recent labels, retrain, compare slices, and canary the candidate.

responses.label: Repair logging before learning
responses.detail: Restore exposure joins, quarantine the gap, and backfill only defensible records.
